title: Rapid, Scalable Assembly and Loading of Bioactive Proteins and Immunostimulants into Diverse Synthetic Nanocarriers Via Flash Nanoprecipitation
protocol: Dissolve 10 g of MeO-PEG17-OH in 200 mL of toluene within a 3-neck round bottom flask under magnetic stirring at 600 rpm.
Connect the 3-neck RBF to a Dean-Stark apparatus attached to a condenser, and maintain inert gas conditions.
Heat the system to 165 °C while stirring at 600 rpm for azeotropic distillation to remove trace water and 100 mL of toluene.
Cool the solution to room temperature after removing from heat.
Add 5.6 mL of triethylamine (3 molar eq.) and 300 mL of anhydrous toluene to the cooled solution while stirring at 600 rpm in an ice bath.
Dilute 3.1 mL of methanesulfonyl chloride (3 molar eq.) in 30 mL of toluene, then slowly add it to the 3-neck RBF via an addition funnel under inert gas conditions.
Stir the mixture overnight at room temperature and 600 rpm under inert conditions.
Filter the solution through a Buchner funnel packed with diatomaceous earth to remove salts.
Remove toluene from the filtered solution using a rotary evaporator set at 40 °C, rotating at 120 rpm, and pressure between 50-100 millibar.
Re-dissolve product in 200 mL of dichloromethane.
Filter through a Buchner funnel packed with diatomaceous earth.
Remove dichloromethane via rotary evaporator set to 40 °C, rotation at 120 rpm, and pressure between 450-600 millibar.
Re-dissolve product in 100% DCM.
Precipitate product by adding dropwise to 500 mL of ice-cold diethyl ether while stirring at 300 rpm.
Decant or aspirate to remove diethyl ether from precipitated product.
Store precipitated product overnight in a vacuum desiccator to dry completely.
Use product immediately or store under inert gas at -20 °C for several months.
Dissolve 5 g of MeO-PEG17-Ms in 200 mL of anhydrous dimethylformamide.
Stir solution at 600 rpm at room temperature under inert gas.
Add 2.5 g of potassium carbonate to stirring solution.
Dilute 1.3 mL of thioacetic acid in 100 mL of anhydrous DMF and add dropwise to the solution via addition funnel.
Stir vigorously overnight at room temperature.
Maintain stirring overnight when forming salt in the solution.
Filter solution through a Buchner funnel packed with diatomaceous earth.
Remove DMF via rotary evaporator set to 60 °C, rotating at 120 rpm and pressure between 5-15 millibar.
Dissolve product in 100 mL of tetrahydrofuran (THF) and add to a column packed with neutral alumina.
Remove THF via rotary evaporator set to 40 °C, rotating at 120 rpm and pressure between 200-300 millibar.
Re-dissolve product in 100% dichloromethane (DCM).
Filter solution through a 6 μm pore size filter paper if salt precipitate forms.
Slowly precipitate the product by adding dropwise to ice-cold diethyl ether, stirring at 300 rpm.
Chill diethyl ether further to -20 °C if precipitate does not form.
Decant or aspirate to remove diethyl ether from the precipitated product.
Store the product overnight in a vacuum desiccator and subsequently under inert gas at -20 °C.
Dissolve MeO-PEG17-TA in 10 mL of anhydrous DMF within a Schlenk flask under argon while stirring at 400 rpm.
Add 1.1 molar eq of sodium methoxide (0.5 M solution in methanol) to the solution and stir for 5 minutes.
Add 35 molar eq of propylene sulfide rapidly to the mixture, then stir for 10 minutes.
Add 10 molar eq of glacial acetic acid to the mixture and stir for 5 minutes.
Remove DMF via rotary evaporation with water bath set at 60°C, rotation at 120 rpm, and pressure between 5-15 millibar.
Redissolve product in DCM and precipitate in methanol.
Centrifuge conical tubes at 7500 x g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Aspirate away supernatant from the centrifuged mixture.
Store product, PEG17-bl-PPS35-SH, overnight in a vacuum desiccator and subsequently under inert gas at -20°C.
Add hydrophobic dyes or drugs to the polymer.
Vortex vigorously to dissolve in 500 µL of THF.
Dissolve hydrophilic cargo in 500 µL of an aqueous buffer.
Add 2.5 mL of an aqueous buffer to a reservoir.
Place the reservoir under the CIJ mixer.
Load impingement solutions into separate syringes.
Insert syringes into Luer-lock adapters at the top of the CIJ mixer.
Depress both syringes simultaneously and with equal force in a single, smooth motion.
Collect outflow in an empty reservoir for multiple sequential impingements.
Split nascent nanostructure solution between two syringes.
Repeat steps 2.6.1-2.6.2 up to 4 more times if performing multiple impingements.
Gently stir collected outflow in the aqueous buffer-filled reservoir to ensure mixing.
Dialyze nanocarrier formulation in the same aqueous buffer used for impingement, using tubing of an appropriate MW cutoff for at least 24 hours with at least 2 buffer changes.
Filter formulation through a size exclusion or desalting/buffer exchange column using 1x PBS as the aqueous buffer.
Remove volatile organic solvent using vacuum desiccation overnight.
Filter the formulation using a tangential flow filtration system with a 50-100 kDa filter.
Concentrate the nanocarrier formulation using a spin concentrator system.
Resuspend the nanocarriers between spins if necessary.
Reduce the volume of the nanocarrier formulation using vacuum desiccation.
Store the nanocarriers at 4 °C for weeks to months.
Vortex the nanocarrier formulations briefly before use after storage.
Measure loading efficiency using a fluorimeter or spectrophotometer.
Disrupt PEG-bl-PPS nanostructures by adding 25 μL of the formulation to an equal volume of either 1% H2O2 or 1% Triton X-100.
Separate and distinguish cargo from polymer absorbance via high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) using a size exclusion column compatible with aqueous buffers.
Lyophilize the formulation by freezing 100 μL in a 1.5 mL plastic tube at -80 °C overnight.
Place the frozen tube into a glass vacuum container and place onto a lyophilizer.
Allow 24 hours for lyophilization to occur.
Re-dissolve the lyophilized material in 50 μL of DMF or THF prior to separation and detection via HPLC.
Measure nanocarrier size using dynamic light scattering (DLS).
Determine nanocarrier morphology using cryogenic transmission electron microscopy (cryoTEM).
Machine multi-layered instrument chassis from ¾” acrylic sheets and assemble.
3D print parts with polylactide (PLA) plastic.
Print the syringe expulsion (SE) 2-part apparatus: SE part 1 - Rear FNP block holding carriage and SE part 2 - Front Expulsion guide.
Print the infrared sensor braces.
Fasten instrument chassis layers together with M5 hex bolts and add rubber feet to the base.
Configure a single-board computer with Raspbian GNU/Linux 8.0 (Jessie) operating system.
Download all dependencies specified in the README file after receiving the zipped software package.
Install a 24 V brushed DC motor.
Mount a precision slide to the instrument base.
Remove the threaded rod temporarily.
Mount the slide using two #8-32 flat machine screws.
Mount DC motor to precision slide using screw beam coupling.
Assemble expulsion platform from metal plates and L-shaped corner braces.
Mount base metal platform to sliding platform using #6-32 screws.
Attach linear motion pillow blocks onto M8 chrome-plated stainless-steel rails.
Thread rails through linear shaft guide/support and lock rails.
Mount SE parts 1 and 2 onto pillow blocks using M4 machine screws.
Loosely join SE parts 1 and 2 with M8 hex bolts.
Configure space between SE part 1 and 2 with helical compression springs secured by nylon bushings.
Wire circuit, connecting the motor controller to I2C/SDA, 3.3 V, and GND pins on the single board computer.
Connect DC motor terminals to the M- and M+ blocks of the motor controller board.
Connect the 24 V, 2.5 A power supply to the V+ and GND blocks of the motor controller.
Connect the 3V3 and 5V pins of the motor control board to the respective pins on the single board computer.
Connect SDA and SCL pins of the motor controller to pins 3 and 5 of the single board computer, respectively.
Route front infrared proximity sensor wiring to RPi GPIO pin 24.
Route rear infrared proximity sensor wiring to RPi GPIO pin 23.
Snap the wired IR sensors into 3D-printed infrared sensor braces.
Mount the sensor braces onto the instrument base.
Connect a 7” touchscreen LCD display to the 5V, GND, and display serial interface pins of the single board computer.
Use auto run mode on the custom-made high-speed syringe pump system.
Allow the motor to automatically position the syringe expulsion platform to the beginning of the precision slide.
Ensure that the path in front of and behind the metal plate is clear.
Load 1 mL plastic syringes as described in section 2.5.
Mount the loaded syringes onto the female Luer connectors of the CIJ mixer.
Load the CIJ mixer (with syringes attached) into the rectangular opening of the rear expulsion carriage.
Set the desired motor speed using the slider in the GUI.
Ensure a flow rate of at least 1 mL/s for the CIJ mixer channel dimensions provided.
Adjust the flow rate and channel diameter as needed to maintain an appropriate Reynolds number for turbulent mixing.
Advance the syringe plungers with a perpendicular metal plate moving along a high-precision aluminum slide coupled to the motor shaft.
Route the capillary tubing outlet from the CIJ mixer into an appropriate collection container.
Press the Run button in the software interface to expel reactants from syringes into the CIJ mixer.
Use manual run mode by pressing the forward button continuously through the completion of the run.
Use manual platform positioning mode by running the motor at low speed (20% power) in response to the forward and reverse buttons on the software interface.
